key_insight: KaliBench shows that translating natural language into exact, executable Kali Linux commands is much harder than standard cybersecurity benchmarks suggest, especially without explicit tool hints.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark provides a deterministic, verifiable way to train and evaluate AI agents for real-world cybersecurity tool use, where small CLI mistakes can break execution.
method: Spans 23 capability dimensions across 5 security phases
Uses canonicalization, alias-aware evaluation, sandboxed execution, and human review for verification
evidence_signal: Across 24 model configurations, no open-weight model exceeded 42% exact-command accuracy in the unrestricted setting, but fine-tuning and verifiable-reward RL improved an 8B model substantially.
watch_item: Because the benchmark relies on CLI exactness and sandboxed verification, performance may not fully capture robustness to real-world environment variation or unseen tool versions.
paper_title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
